methodologyNote: Accuracy-first educational museum seed. Prefer null over invention. Every specification carries a confidence tag. No operational targeting, construction recipes, or lethality-optimization content.

description.en: Twin-engine, two-seat air-superiority fighter. Iran is the only foreign customer. Ordered under Project Persian King in 1974 and delivered from 1976, Iranian Tomcats retained AWG-9 radar and AIM-54 Phoenix capability. After 1979 and the U.S. embargo, IRIAF sustained a reduced fleet through domestic maintenance and flew them extensively in the Iran–Iraq War.

historicalContext.en: Selected partly to counter high-altitude Soviet MiG-25 overflights. Contracts covered 80 aircraft; sources agree 79 were delivered and the 80th retained in the United States.

technologicalSignificance.en: Only non-U.S. Tomcat operator; AWG-9/Phoenix suite drove decades of Iranian sustainment effort.
